data.title: Chat watcher: a board message starts a loop of ticks that runs until the company is dry, not a single tick

data.to:
Board directive, Claude Code chat (metawork), 2026-09-10, verbatim: "when I send a message, it should trigger a loop, not a tick". Stop rule chosen by the board the same day: UNTIL THE COMPANY RUNS DRY. Filed explicitly by the board in that channel (the CLAUDE.md exception), so this is a board-authored task.

WHAT CHANGES. Today apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs fires exactly one headless tick per human message: decide() sees the sentinel (last-human-message.json) above the highwater, arms the 15s debounce, fires one claude -p /advance with a fresh nonce+lock, and settle() releases the lock and writes the highwater. Then it waits for the next human message. Consequence the board has lived: a message that needs three lifecycle stages (plan -> implement -> review) advances one stage and then the company sits idle until he speaks again; msg 607 got no ack for 40 minutes because its one tick was spent on AS-91.

TARGET. A human message opens a LOOP: after a fired tick settles, the watcher immediately evaluates a continue-predicate and fires the next tick (fresh nonce, fresh lock, same single-flight discipline) while it holds; it stops when the company is dry. The loop is a property of the watcher, not of the tick — /advance stays one bounded tick and knows nothing about the loop.

CONTINUE-PREDICATE (the board picked the "runs dry" rule; make it a pure, exported, unit-tested function like decide()/decideDeploy(), and record the reason in the log on every evaluation):
  continue when ANY of:
    (a) a task is in_planning, planned, in_progress or review (something is mid-lifecycle);
    (b) a backlog task is READY under the scheduling rule (no unmet depends_on; Chat set first while it is non-empty per CLAUDE.md "Scheduling priority");
    (c) the sentinel is above the highwater again (a new human message arrived during the last tick — already the existing fire path; the loop must not double-fire it).
  stop when ANY of:
    (d) none of (a)/(b)/(c) hold — the company is dry (needs_human/blocked tasks do not count as work; they are waiting on the board);
    (e) NO-PROGRESS GUARD: two consecutive ticks ended without a new commit on master (compare HEAD before/after each tick) — a tick that no-ops twice is stuck, not working; stop and log which condition it saw;
    (f) SAFETY CAP: 24 consecutive ticks or 8 hours of continuous looping per human message, whichever first — logged as cap-hit; a new message re-arms;
    (g) the tick child exited non-zero or was killed by the 30-min tick timeout twice in a row.
  Reading task state: the watcher is node:* builtins only and must not shell out to the lattice CLI per tick; read .lattice/tasks/*.json directly (status, priority, depends_on via the relationships the CLI writes) — that file layout is the CLI's own storage and the AS-8/AS-27 code already reads .lattice read-only. Compute readiness = every depends_on target is done/cancelled.

CONSTRAINTS. Zero new dependencies. Single-flight is unchanged: one tick at a time, one lock, the deploy poll's rule 1 still refuses under a fresh lock; the loop must not starve the deploy poll (decide between ticks whether a deploy is pending — if deploy-state says stale-build and docker is available, let one deploy run before the next tick, so a merge in tick N is live before tick N+1 reviews anything on 8347). Heartbeat/lock/highwater semantics unchanged (AS-16 nonce per fire). The UI's loop indicator (AS-27) should read "Loop active" while the watcher is looping: write source:"watcher-loop" or an explicit loop marker the loop-status derivation understands, and extend describeLoopStatus so the sidebar distinguishes a single watcher tick from a watcher loop, with the tick count (e.g. "Loop active - watcher, tick 3"). Every stop reason is logged in launchd.out and surfaced in loop-status's lastTick/lastLoop fields so the board can see WHY the company stopped.

RELATION TO AS-84: the lock-ownership question (pid vs source) is shared; do not fork the semantics — if AS-84 lands first, build on it; if this lands first, keep lock handling byte-identical and leave AS-84's scope alone.

ACCEPTANCE (M4-shaped: each property names its falsifier, satisfied by an OBSERVED red):
  AC-1 shouldContinue() is pure and exported; every rule (a)-(g) has a unit test that turns RED when that rule is deleted or its comparison inverted (one mutation per rule, exact failing set recorded).
  AC-2 the no-progress guard: a fixture where HEAD does not move across two ticks stops the loop; deleting the guard turns the test red.
  AC-3 the cap: a fixture at 24 ticks stops; 23 continues.
  AC-4 readiness: a backlog task with an unmet depends_on is NOT counted as ready; deleting the depends_on check turns it red.
  AC-5 a new human message mid-loop is delivered exactly once (no double fire): sentinel advance during tick N is consumed by tick N+1's normal inbox pull and the highwater moves once; a test asserts one fire, not two.
  AC-6 loop-status: the sidebar label for a watcher loop is observed over the served endpoint with a tick count; the label test goes red when the loop branch is removed.
  AC-7 one observed end-to-end run on an isolated stack (own compose project, temp data dir, fixture .lattice): one human message -> at least three consecutive ticks -> stop with reason "dry" logged; and a second run stopping on the no-progress guard.
  AC-8 --build receipt on every counted suite run (Image ... Built line quoted); cardinality before quantification vs the master baseline.
  AC-9 README (apps/chat/watch/README.md) documents the loop, the stop rules, the cap, and how to read the stop reason.
  AC-10 the unguarded main() wiring is enumerated in the implementation report (AS-82 hole), capped small; all logic is module-scope exports.

METAWORK ALREADY APPLIED WITH THIS FILING: CLAUDE.md "Target interface" paragraph updated to the loop semantics. .claude/commands/advance.md is unchanged — one invocation is still one tick.

data.body: Ordering note (board, at filing): AS-84 is NOT a hard dependency. The description allows either order, and the depends_on edge added at filing was removed for that reason. The Chat-set scheduling rule and the recorded CTO order (AS-84 + AS-88 near the front) decide sequencing; the CTO may reorder in planning.

CTO ordering call, 2026-09-10 (tick watcher:17217:26a2eb602b99ba56), under the within-set ordering authority the board delegated in DM msg 614 ('your call').

DECISION: AS-95 moves to SECOND in the critical Chat set, immediately after AS-94. Priority unchanged (critical). The rule becomes: AS-94 first, AS-95 second, then the rest of the set by age.

Why it moves. By the age tiebreak, sixteen Chat-set tasks sit ahead of this one (AS-28, AS-61, AS-72, AS-73, AS-74, AS-80, AS-81, AS-82, AS-83, AS-84, AS-85, AS-86, AS-87, AS-88, AS-89, AS-92 — AS-94 excluded because it goes first regardless). Each task is three lifecycle stages plus a merge, i.e. three to four ticks; under the current watcher that is one tick per board message, so the loop mechanism would arrive after roughly fifty to sixty messages from the board. The board has now asked for the loop twice — the 2026-09-10 Claude Code directive that filed this task, and DM msg 632 'loop on those until done' — and the second ask was made in the belief that the mechanism exists. It does not. The task that converts one message into the whole queue is worth more than any single item in that queue: landed second, every later Chat-set task costs the board one message instead of four; landed by age, the loop arrives when there is almost nothing left to loop over. That is the entire argument; nothing in the queue ahead of it is a live defect the board can see (they are guard holes, harness hangs, a favicon, and the AS-75 F-series).

Why not FIRST. AS-94 is a one-plan task that ends in a needs_human for the launchctl bootstrap, and it is the second half of the outcome the board asked for 'right away' in DM msg 607 (links that answer from the phone). It enters planning this tick. Putting AS-95 ahead of it buys nothing — AS-94's planning tick is already spent — and would leave the phone links dead for the whole of AS-95's build.

Interaction the planner must respect. Rule (b) of this task's continue-predicate reads the CLAUDE.md scheduling rule to decide readiness. Do NOT hard-code task ids: encode the within-set ordering as data (a named-first list, then age) so the next CTO ordering call is a data change, not a watcher edit. Also: this decision makes AS-96 (cancelled this tick) a worked example of why rule (b) must treat depends_on targets in status cancelled as satisfied AND must not treat a cancelled task as ready — check both directions in AC-4.

PROPOSED CLAUDE.md WORDING (employees never edit CLAUDE.md; the orchestrator applies). In section 'Scheduling priority', replace the sentence beginning 'Standing rule (CTO call, delegated by the board in DM msg 614, 2026-09-09, "your call"): AS-93 ... says so in its report.' with:

'Standing rule (CTO call, delegated by the board in DM msg 614, 2026-09-09, "your call"; revised 2026-09-10 from DM msg 632): AS-94 (supervise the Lattice dashboard under launchd) goes first, then AS-95 (a board message starts a loop of ticks until the company is dry), then the rest of the set by age. AS-94 is the second half of the outcome the board asked for "right away" (DM msg 607; the first half, AS-93, merged 2026-09-10 as f15c4ad). AS-95 jumps the age queue because the board has asked for the loop twice (the 2026-09-10 Claude Code directive that filed it, and DM msg 632 "loop on those until done") and because by age it sat behind sixteen Chat-set tasks — at three to four ticks per task, that is fifty-plus board messages before the mechanism that lets one message drive the whole queue; landed second, every task after it costs the board one message instead of four. A tick that would start any other Chat-set task while AS-94 or AS-95 is ready picks them instead and says so in its report. Retired rule, kept for the record: AS-93 went first (merged 2026-09-10, f15c4ad).'

Also in that section, the sentence 'AS-55 and AS-79 are chat-adjacent but board-gated, so they are not in the set.' gains: 'AS-96 was cancelled 2026-09-10 (the dashboard port question moved upstream to the Lattice project, DM msg 632).'

Planner breadcrumb (cto-owen, headless tick, 2026-09-10): plan written against master 860dfca. Shape: shouldContinue({board, sentinel, highwater, loop, tick, now, limits}) pure+exported, stop rules evaluated first (g failures, e no-progress, f cap) then continue rules (c new-message, a mid-lifecycle, b ready-backlog), else dry. readBoard() reads .lattice/tasks/*.json over injected fs; dependsOn = own relationships_out depends_on UNION other tasks' blocks pointing at it (relationships_in is only in show --json, not in the file). headOf() reads .git/HEAD without shelling out. Loop state in memory, mirrored to advance-loop.json (lastLoop keeps the stop reason); a watcher restart resumes an active loop with tick count carried forward. Lock body gains loop:{ticks} but source stays 'watcher' and makeLockOps is untouched (AS-84 scope preserved); deriveLoopStatus gets a 'watcher-loop' state, sidebar label 'Loop active - watcher, tick N'. Loop yields to a pending deploy between ticks. Mutant table with predicted red sets per rule, isolated e2e recipe for AC-7, AS-82 main() wiring capped at four items. Not verified: makeLockOps/makeDeployOps internals and loadConfig env names (section 8). Complexity high, ~3 ticks. Branch slug: feat/AS-95-watcher-loop.

Implementation progress (developer-marcus, watcher-fired tick, 20:40Z). Branch feat/AS-95-watcher-loop, 3 commits on top of 860dfca: aecc8b8 (pure exports + tests), a3292a1 (main() wiring), d77e289 (lock-marker pins).

DONE and committed: plan §2.2 shouldContinue() + readyBacklog(), §2.3 readBoard()/headOf(), §2.4 all four main() wiring items, §6 commits 1 and 2. shouldContinue evaluates stop rules (failures -> no-progress -> cap) before work rules (new-message -> mid-lifecycle -> backlog-ready -> dry), returns {continue,reason,detail,loop}. readBoard is pure over injected fs, computes dependsOn from depends_on plus the inverse of other tasks' blocks edges, skips unparsable files with a count, never throws. headOf reads .git/HEAD -> loose ref -> packed-refs, follows a gitdir: pointer, returns null on failure.

Two decisions the plan left open, both taken the boring way and both testable: (1) an unreadable HEAD (null) counts as NO progress, so two unknown heads stop the loop — a stop is cheap (a message re-arms) and a runaway is not; (2) §8's open question resolved — acquireLock gains an optional additive second arg (extra fields spread into the body); makeLockOps' acquire/release/stale logic and source:'watcher' are untouched, pinned by lock-marker-absent. makeDeployOps gains pendingDeploy() reading the last evaluate() decision (reason busy|stale-build, and false when docker is unresolvable so the loop never waits forever).

TESTS: apps/chat/test/watcher-loop.test.js, 37 cases. Watcher-related suite (watcher, watcher-loop, loop-status, loop-label, deploy-shape) = 100 tests, 100 pass, 0 fail — NODE --TEST GRADE, not compose. docker is denied in this tick environment (the known headless residual), so no --build receipt and no counted compose number this stage; the next implementer or QA must run the counted compose suite with --build and an isolated COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and quote the 'Image ... Built' line. Master baseline count (AC-8) is therefore still unrecorded.

MUTANTS: 12 run on a scratch copy (scratchpad/developer-marcus/AS-95/mutate.mjs, which copies the two files out of the worktree — the worktree was never mutated; every run ended 'restored: true'). All 12 died, no survivors. Red sets matched the plan's §3 predictions except one honest deviation worth recording: mutant c ('>' -> '>=' on the new-message compare) was predicted to red c-new-message; observed it reds c-equal-not-new plus 9 others (the shared fixture uses sentinel 10 == highwater 10) while c-new-message stays green — the guard is proven, but by a different case than the plan named. f-23 stayed green as the plan predicted.

REMAINING for the next implementer: §2.6 (server.js loopState -> deriveLoopStatus 'watcher-loop' + describeLoopStatus label, loop-status/loop-label tests) = commit 3; §5 README section = commit 4 (keep it as a NEW section — AS-94 is editing apps/chat/watch/README.md in a parallel lane); AC-5's c-single-fire (the loop must not double-fire when decide() already fired — poll() returns immediately after the fire branch, but it is asserted only by reading, not by a test); AC-7's isolated end-to-end recipe with a fake claude binary; a unit test for pendingDeploy(); and the counted compose run. Note for §4: loadConfig has no claudeBin/data-dir env override beyond ADVANCE_* — verify names before writing the e2e.

Implementation progress (developer-marcus, watcher-fired tick watcher:17217:6cadb7a56edccd3f, 2026-09-10 ~21:05Z). Branch feat/AS-95-watcher-loop, worktree .worktrees/AS-95, tree CLEAN.

COMMITS ADDED THIS TICK (on top of aecc8b8 / a3292a1 / d77e289):
  958a44c  loop-status watcher-loop state and sidebar label (plan 2.6)
  990e78c  make the single-fire guarantee an exported function, not statement order (AC-5)
  b549f5e  README - the loop, its stop rules, and how to read the stop reason (plan 5, AC-9)

DONE against the remaining list from my 20:38Z comment:
- plan 2.6 COMPLETE. deriveLoopStatus gains loopState and a fifth state 'watcher-loop', plus a loop:{active,ticks,startedAt,armedBy,lastLoop} field built field-by-field (nonce/detail never ride out). describeLoopStatus renders 'Loop active - watcher, tick N' and, when idle, one sentence naming why the last loop stopped. server.js reads apps/chat/data/advance-loop.json with the same degradation contract as the other three files there, and the SSE change-key now includes loop.ticks so a new loop tick earns a push frame.
- AC-5 c-single-fire COMPLETE, and better than planned - see DECISIONS below.
- pendingDeploy() unit test COMPLETE (in watcher.test.js, beside the existing deployHarness rather than duplicating that harness), including its falsifier: with no docker binary a stale build is permanent, so pendingDeploy() must report false or the loop waits forever.
- plan 5 README COMPLETE as a NEW section 'AS-95: a message starts a loop, not a tick' (AS-94 is editing the same README in a parallel lane; new section = no merge fight), plus one row added to the Files table.

STILL REMAINING (both deferred to QA, see below): AC-7's isolated end-to-end run, and AC-8's counted compose run.

TEST NUMBERS - node --test grade (docker DENIED by the sandbox in this tick; see below). Cardinality before quantification: master baseline 293 tests, branch 340 tests, delta +47 (this tick added 10 new cases; the rest are the previous two commits'). Branch: 340 tests, 340 pass, 0 fail. Master: 293/293/0.

MUTANTS RUN THIS TICK - 10 AC-6 mutants over lib/loop-status.js, public/loop-status.js and server.js, on a SCRATCH COPY of apps/chat (scratchpad/developer-marcus/AS-95/mutate-ac6.mjs; the worktree was never mutated), each asserted applied before the run and the restore proved afterwards. ALL 10 RED, none survived; baseline after restore green (67/67 over the three observing files). Red sets (distinct test names):
  AC-6.1 remove the watcher-loop branch          -> derive-watcher-loop, api-loop-status
  AC-6.2 lock marker stops counting as a witness -> derive-watcher-loop
  AC-6.3 mirror file stops counting              -> derive-watcher-loop, api-loop-status
  AC-6.4 loop object never derived               -> derive-watcher-loop, displaces, lastLoop, api-loop-status (4)
  AC-6.5 lastLoop dropped                        -> lastLoop, api-loop-status
  AC-6.6 remove the watcher-loop label case      -> label-watcher-loop
  AC-6.7 label ignores the lock marker           -> label-watcher-loop
  AC-6.8 tone not mapped (unstyled dot)          -> label-watcher-loop
  AC-6.9 stop-reason sentence never rendered     -> label-stopped-loop
  AC-6.10 server never reads advance-loop.json   -> api-loop-status
Note the pair AC-6.2/AC-6.3: each witness is proven load-bearing on its own, so neither is decoration.

DECISIONS I TOOK THAT THE PLAN LEFT OPEN:
1. AC-5 was going to be a spy-on-fire test over main(). main() is not exercisable without child processes, and the real guarantee was 'one if sits above another in poll()' - a property held by statement layout, which no test can hold and the next edit can silently lose. So I extracted nextPollAction({decideAction, loopPending, deployPending}) -> 'fire-message'|'fire-loop'|'wait-deploy'|'idle', pure and exported, as the ONE place the two paths are ordered; poll() now calls it. Enumerated over all 16 input combinations: at most one fire per poll, and decideAction==='fire' always wins. This REDUCES the unguarded main() surface (AC-10) rather than adding to it - it is the only structural change beyond plan 2.4's four items.
2. 'watcher-loop' is a fifth STATE but maps to the existing green 'loop' TONE. A new tone would render .loop-dot--watcher-loop, for which there is no CSS rule, i.e. an invisible dot. Mapping in describeLoopStatus (toneFor) keeps the dot correct even if derivation and CSS ever ship apart. Asserted.
3. Two independent witnesses for 'this tick belongs to a loop' - advance-loop.json's active flag OR the lock's loop.ticks marker - either sufficient. Requiring both would report a live loop as a bare tick whenever one lagged (the file is a poll behind a just-fired tick; a pre-AS-95 lock has no marker). The label prefers the lock's number (it IS the tick being reported) and falls back to the file.
4. Three existing AS-27 assertions changed because the payload shape grew: tick now carries loopTicks, and the status object carries loop. Those are deepEqual whitelists on what reaches the client (the AS-16 nonce guard), so they had to be updated deliberately rather than loosened - they still enumerate every key.

AC-8 / docker: attempted ONCE from inside the worktree's apps/chat with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=asc-as95-marcus-test and the absolute /usr/local/bin/docker that deploy-state.json reports. The sandbox DENIED the command outright (not a daemon error - the Bash tool refused it), as it did a plain 'docker version' probe. So there is NO --build receipt from this tick and NO valid compose count: every number above is node --test grade and must not be quoted as a compose number.

READY FOR REVIEW: yes, with two items explicitly deferred to QA, who has docker:
  (1) AC-8 - the counted compose run with --build, quoting the 'Image ... Built' line. Expect ~340 in the container if compose runs the same file set; a smaller number means a stale image, not a smaller suite.
  (2) AC-7 - the isolated end-to-end run (plan 4: temp .lattice fixture, fake claude binary, own compose project). I did not write the recipe script this tick - I ran out of box. The plan's 4 is precise enough to execute as written; note that plan 8 flagged the env-override names as unverified, and I can confirm main() reads its data dir and repo root from config, so the recipe's ADVANCE_* knobs need checking against loadConfig() before the run.
M6 note for the reviewer: the plan's own 7 names five probes worth more than the criteria list - a message landing in the same poll as a loop continue (now answerable directly against nextPollAction), a restart between settle() and the loop fire, a stale lock left by a SIGKILLed tick while the loop believes it is active, packed-refs HEAD, and a task file caught mid-write.

Orchestrator (cto-owen, tick watcher:17217:6cadb7a56edccd3f): implementation stage closed at Marcus's recommendation — 6 commits on feat/AS-95-watcher-loop (aecc8b8 a3292a1 d77e289 958a44c 990e78c b549f5e), node --test grade 340/340 vs master 293 (+47), 22 mutants red across two ticks, no survivors. Moved to review. QA (fresh context, has docker) owns the two deferred items as part of the review: AC-8 counted compose run with --build (quote the 'Image ... Built' line, cardinality vs master 293 first) and AC-7 the isolated end-to-end run per plan §4 — verify the ADVANCE_* env-override names against loadConfig() before writing the e2e (plan §8 flag). Review also checks Marcus's four open-decision calls (nextPollAction() as the AC-5 carrier; watcher-loop mapped to the green loop tone; two independent loop witnesses; three AS-27 deepEqual whitelists widened). AS-94's parallel README edit is unmerged — reviewer notes any merge seam in apps/chat/watch/README.md.

data.body:
QA review — qa-priya, 2026-09-10, live session (docker available). Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION-LEVEL REWORK NEEDED.
Reviewed cold: plan, description (board-authored), `git diff master...feat/AS-95-watcher-loop` (10 files, +1312/-26), README, tests. Not read before my findings were written: the implementer's comments (read afterwards for AC-10 only) and the auto-review (it FAILED — timed out at 600s, no artifact, no findings; nothing to compare).
Repro material: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/ (e2e/lib.sh + run1..run7 dirs, mut/ mutants, compose-*.log). Isolated stack: temp git repo with a 3-task fixture .lattice, fake `claude` shell binary, own data dir, ADVANCE_POLL_S=1, ADVANCE_DEBOUNCE_S=1, ADVANCE_CHAT_URL=127.0.0.1:1 — never touched apps/chat/data or asc-chat.

== FINDINGS FIRST (8 outside the criteria list; 2 blocking) ==

F1 BLOCKING — a loop tick that loses the lock kills the loop silently. poll() clears loopPending and calls fire(); fire() aborts on acquireLock failure without settle()/settleLoop(), so nothing ever re-evaluates. OBSERVED (run3: tick 1 hands the lock to a live foreign pid, i.e. a /loop or manual session winning the race the shared lock exists for): `LOOP-FIRE tick 2` -> `SKIP fire aborted: lock acquisition failed` -> silence for 12 polls; T1 still in_progress; advance-loop.json frozen at active:true ticks:1 lastLoop:null; no LOOP-STOP. Violates the description's "Every stop reason is logged in launchd.out and surfaced in loop-status ... so the board can see WHY the company stopped" — the company stops with work remaining and the sidebar says a loop is active. The message path self-heals (highwater not yet written -> decide() refires); the loop path must too: keep loopPending on an aborted fire (retry next poll, one SKIP line per episode) or fold the abort into settleLoop as a stop with a reason. Needs its own M4 falsifier.

F2 BLOCKING — LOOP-RESUME after an unclean watcher death fires over the orphan's lock: two ticks at once. loadLoopState sets loopPending; the startup poll fires; the lock carries the DEAD watcher's pid -> isLockStale dead-pid -> STEAL -> second claude while the first (orphaned, not killed on SIGKILL/crash — shutdown() only runs on SIGTERM/SIGINT) still runs. OBSERVED (run4b: kill -9 during tick 2, relaunch): `LOOP-RESUME` -> `LOOP-FIRE tick 2` -> `STEAL stale lock (dead-pid, pid 36777)` -> two fake ticks alive concurrently for ~5s, 3s after relaunch, unconditionally. Pre-AS-95 the same steal needed a human message plus the debounce; AS-95 makes it automatic. The lock code is byte-identical as required, but "Single-flight is unchanged: one tick at a time" is not true in behaviour. Minimal in-scope fix without touching makeLockOps: on resume, do not fire while a lock file exists younger than tickTimeoutMin (age, not pid liveness), and log the wait; the pid-vs-source ownership question stays AS-84's.

F3 — a watcher death during tick 1 loses the loop entirely: writeLoopState runs only at settle, so no advance-loop.json exists yet. OBSERVED (run4: kill -9 during tick 1, relaunch): no LOOP-RESUME, orphan finishes, T1 in_progress, dead-pid lock left, watcher idle until the next message — the exact symptom this task exists to fix, in the crash case. Follows the plan as written ("mirrored after every evaluation"), so plan gap not implementer error; one call to writeLoopState() at LOOP-START closes it. Non-blocking; include in the rework.

F4 — every loop tick waits up to one deploy-poll interval (60s in production) even with nothing to deploy. pendingDeploy() is true on reason 'busy', and the deploy poll during any tick always says busy; after settle the loop reports LOOP-WAIT until the next deploy poll clears it. OBSERVED (run6b, deploy poll 4s, docker=/usr/bin/true): ticks 2, 3 and 4 each logged `LOOP-WAIT deploy pending` then fired 1-2s later; also stays pending after a completed deploy until the following poll. Bounded, never a hang; the yield itself works as specified (run6b tick 1 -> LOOP-WAIT -> DEPLOY building -> fail/cooldown -> LOOP-FIRE tick 2, deploy strictly between ticks). Description says "immediately". Non-blocking; a settle-time evaluate({busy:false}) would remove the tax. Backlog-worthy if not taken in the rework.

F5 — sidebar reads Idle between loop ticks: deriveLoopStatus returns 'idle' with loop.active:true whenever no fresh lock exists (encoded in the tests), so during the between-tick gap (F4 makes it up to ~65s) the label is "Idle" while a loop is armed. AC-6 as written is met; the description's "read 'Loop active' while the watcher is looping" is not, between ticks. Non-blocking; one branch in describeLoopStatus.

F6 — docs/log trivia, not fixed inline because the verdict is rework: README example shows `LOOP-START` then `LOOP-FIRE tick 1`; tick 1 is fired by the message path (`FIRE messageId N`) and LOOP-FIRE appears only for loop ticks 2+ (run1 log). Also a loop tick logs `FIRE messageId 2 from human:forrest` (run5) — reads as a message fire. Also the poll() comment says a loop tick "re-uses the current highwater id"; it passes the real sentinel (correct, and load-bearing for AC-5).

F7 — AC-10 is only partly met. Unguarded main() additions: 142 lines (my count from the diff; pure section 219, lock/deploy ops 15), including three new inner functions carrying policy — settleLoop (fold verdict, stop-on-error, lastLoop), loadLoopState (resume policy: counters reset, pending), writeLoopState — plus the fire()/poll() loop-pending handling. The report enumerates by reference to the plan's four items, not by line, and the plan's cap was those four items. Both blocking defects (F1, F2) live in this unguarded region and neither has a unit falsifier. F5 — TAKEN. The sidebar reading "Idle" between loop ticks is the board-visible half of this task, and the gap is exactly when the board looks. deriveLoopStatus now reports watcher-loop when there is no fresh lock but the mirror says active AND the watcher heartbeat is fresh — the heartbeat guard matters, because a mirror left active:true by a watcher killed mid-loop would otherwise claim a live loop forever (that case now reads off). The detail line says which gap the reader is in, and C5's "a running loop reads as idle in that gap" sentence is dropped for watcher loops (it still applies to a session /loop, which nothing mirrors). Falsifiers f5-between-ticks, f5-needs-a-live-watcher, f5-does-not-touch-the-lock-states, f5-between-ticks-label, f5-idle-keeps-its-own-words; mutants m-f5-idle-between and m-f5-no-heartbeat-guard red.

F4 — NOT TAKEN, deliberately. pendingDeploy() is true on reason 'busy', and 'busy' means the deploy poll never got to work out whether a rebuild is owed. Treating it as not-pending would fire tick N+1 against the pre-merge container, which is the exact guarantee the yield exists for. The only real fix is to let the loop KICK a deploy evaluation at settle instead of waiting for the 60s poll — and evaluate() is async, has no re-entrancy guard (deploying is set two awaits deep, inside performDeploy), shells out to git, probes the container, and can exit(70) to restart the watcher. Having the loop drive it is a new cross-component interaction in a component this plan put out of scope (§1: no change to the deploy ops internals); it needs its own guard and its own falsifiers, and doing it here would be exactly the redesign-under-momentum I am supposed to escalate rather than commit. The cost as it stands is bounded at one deploy-poll interval per loop tick (60s prod) against ticks that run minutes, it is logged once per episode, and it never hangs. Filed as its own task rather than left in a review comment.
